resolved_by: Claude (Anthropic), fixer group G1, 18 Oct 2026 (pending team review)
new_theme: Build L1 (dev): a sync-word detector on a stated 64-bit test bit stream. A repeating Vector Source plays the bits, which are recorded as float 0/1 in bits.dat. An FIR correlator (taps: the sync word 1110 1011 0010 0001, time-reversed and mapped to +-1) feeds a Threshold at 7.5. The threshold writes 1.0 to flags.dat on the last bit of each error-free copy only. Each period of the stream holds one error-free copy and one copy with one wrong bit. v2 cell: data_source|filter|nonlinear -> dev. cluster_id: chain:data_source|filter|nonlinear. compose.audit_items finds no other item in this cell.
deviation_from_plan: The plan's brief built on 'Correlate Access Code - Bit' (digital_correlate_access_code_bb, cell data_source|frame_sync). That block is not in the pinned GNU Radio 3.10.12 GRC catalog. This stage re-checked it in WSL: /usr/share/gnuradio/grc/blocks holds only digital_correlate_access_code_tag_xx ('- Tag') and digital_correlate_access_code_xx_ts ('- Tag Stream'). gnuradio.digital still has a Python class correlate_access_code_bb, but it has no GRC block definition, so a change_graph edit cannot use it, and probe access_code_bb_block fails at V2. The two catalog variants report detections as stream tags or as variable-rate packet payloads, not as a per-bit output. So the item uses the alternative the brief lists: an FIR correlator followed by a threshold, with a float 0/1 flag stream. The planner's pre-check listed that cell as dev and unused. Everything else in the brief is kept: an explicit pattern with one error-free copy and one near-miss copy, no bit errors allowed, exact equal_prefix checks from sample 0 (max_offset 0), a path graph check against a hard-coded output, and mutants for threshold, wrong word, bypass and off-by-one. bits.dat was added as a second observation point. Without it, a flags-only oracle cannot check the stated input: a different input with the same flags (no near-miss copy, plus a detector that allows one error) passes. Probe other_input_lenient shows that it now fails.

accepted.change: Moot after the re-theme (no tone and no clean-up filter). The lesson still applies, and holds: a correct detector has no transient in the checked samples. Every 16-bit window that reaches back before the first bit is at least 7 bits from the sync word, verified this stage; check_pattern asserts that the zero-history flags equal the periodic ones. FIR, FFT, IIR and Rail- or Slicer-decision designs all produce identical flags from sample 0 (variants v1-v4; probes iir_as_fir_correlator and binary_slicer_threshold).

other_changes: This stage: two mutants behaved the same: 'threshold high = 8' and 'bypass corr' both give an all-zero flags.dat. 'bypass corr' was replaced by 'rewire flags_out <- src', the brief's 'detector bypassed: raw bits written'. A wrong-rate mutant was added (FIR decim 2). There are 11 distinct mutants, each killed by the check named in its 'breaks' label; this was verified mutant by mutant.

This stage: new variant v4 (correlator - 7, clamped by a Rail to 0..1): a genuinely different decision stage in the same dev cell. A first version failed V3 because GRC blacklists the block name 'match'; the block was renamed and the variant now passes V5.

This stage: the instruction's sample-rate sentence follows R3. It now reads 'The sample rate does not affect the result, so you can leave the samp_rate variable as it is', so the model knows what to do with the samp_rate variable and nothing unobservable is required. spec_properties: 'sample rate: stated as irrelevant; not checked'.
This stage: the path check also accepts rational_resampler_xxx (1:1 with correlator taps is an FIR), so every catalog block that can realise the correlator passes.
Observation points bits.dat and flags.dat are matched with params.type = float, and the instruction names both file names and item types (R9).

Probes in build.py --probes, all with the expected verdict: the access-code-bb block fails at V2; the Binary Slicer and IIR correlators pass; hard-coded flags fail the graph check; another input with a lenient detector fails on bits.dat.

review.notes records the known limits: the path check can be cheated on purpose with a one-tap FIR; run length is checked as liveness only; samples 192-3903 are not compared. It also records the relation to gbf-dev-03 and the deviation from the plan.
